Billing ownership checks, notifications, activity recording, member and organization repositories, notification kinds, and ID generation need to be understood.

The spec is very detailed. I am extracting requirements from user stories. One story covers workspace ownership handover. The offered member receives an `ownership_handover` notification. Only one offer can be open per workspace at a time.

Offers expire exactly seven days after creation. The offered member can accept regardless of their current role. Upon acceptance, they become the recorded owner and hold that role. The previous owner steps down to admin if still holding owner at that moment. If the accepter already held owner, only the previous owner's role changes. The workspace always has an owner during the handover.

The existing rule that a workspace never loses its last owner must not block the handover. The offered member can decline, which clears the pending offer and allows the owner to make another. The offering owner may withdraw an open offer. Any workspace member can see whether an offer is active and to whom it is addressed. Role changes from acceptance are announced as manual `member.role_changed` events.

The handover itself publishes an `organization.ownership_transferred` event with `fromUserId` and `toUserId`. The audit log records this action on the organization. All events published during acceptance are attributed to the accepting member.

New member alerts go to the new owner. Billing management changes belong to the new owner and are refused to the previous one.

The previous owner, now an admin, can be removed from the workspace like any other admin.

Only the recorded owner may offer or withdraw an ownership handover. A second member who holds the owner role but is not the recorded owner is refused with a PermissionDeniedError.

An offer must target an active member of the same workspace. Unknown users, members from other workspaces, or removed members trigger a NotFoundError. The owner cannot offer to themselves.

Only the offered member may accept or decline an offer. Anyone else acting on it, or acting when no offer is open, receives `"nothing_pending"`. Accepting or declining a lapsed offer returns `"expired"`. A lapsed offer ceases to count as open; it does not block new offers and acting on it changes nothing. Submitting a new offer while one is already open returns `"pending_exists"`. These refusals throw `OwnershipHandoverError`, exported from `src/lib/errors.ts`.

`OwnershipHandoverError` carries a `conflict` code and a `reason` of type `OwnershipHandoverRefusal`, which is `"self" | "pending_exists" | "nothing_pending" | "expired"`. It maps to the `conflict` app error and is recognized as a domain error. An `orgId` outside the actor's workspace triggers a `TenantScopeError` on every operation. Offers are isolated per workspace.

If either party leaves the workspace while an offer is open, it is automatically withdrawn. Offers are persisted and require a new table in freshly migrated databases. The API exports `OwnershipHandoverStatus` and `OwnershipHandover` types from `src/types/organization.ts`.

The `OwnershipHandover` type includes `toUserId`, `expiresAt`, `createdAt`, and `resolvedAt`. `expiresAt` is exactly seven days after `createdAt`. An open offer has status `"pending"` and no `resolvedAt`; resolved offers carry their status and the instant of resolution. The organization service will expose `initiateOwnershipHandover(actor, orgId, toUserId)` returning a `Promise<OwnershipHandover>`.

The organization service will also expose `acceptOwnershipHandover`, `declineOwnershipHandover`, `cancelOwnershipHandover`, and `getPendingOwnershipHandover`. The last returns the open offer or null. A withdrawn offer carries status `"canceled"`. Lapsed offers carry status `"expired"`.

The phrase "acting on it changes nothing" is ambiguous. It could mean the offer record stays unchanged in the database while being treated as expired, or that no ownership transfer occurs at all.

Lapsed offers are treated as expired by time rather than by database status. getPending returns null for them, so they do not block new offers. The spec defines expiry as a time-based rule: an offer can still be acted on before T + 7 days and no longer after.

The phrase "acting on it changes nothing" is now interpreted as the ownership state remaining unchanged, not that the database row stays untouched.
